sources.title: UNESCO, Moidams: the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
sources.note: Description and Outstanding Universal Value, especially brief synthesis, authenticity and continuing rituals. Broad 13th to 19th-century heritage is explicitly inherited context.

sources.title: John M’Cosh, Topography of Assam (1837)
sources.note: Printed pp. 28, 29, 31, 86 and 115, directly searchable full PDF. Colonial observer; descriptive household practices and his own clinical account are attributed. His sweeping racial judgments and medical causation are not adopted.

sources.title: Rana Pratap Behal, Labour Resistance in Indenture Plantations in the Assam Valley (2024)
sources.note: Public chapter summary: Growth of the Tea Industry and The Indentured Labour Regime; only 1872 output and mid-1860s arrangements used, not later workforce totals.

sources.title: Krishna Kanta Handiqui State Open University, Import of labour from Central India
sources.note: Tea World lesson, recruitment, living conditions and Labour Transportation. Description covers developing colonial industry; no undated detail assigned to a precise year.

sources.title: The Missionary Jubilee: American Baptist Missionary Union (1865)
sources.note: Assam mission chronology, 1847 to 1849; paragraph beginning In 1849 (printed page numeral not securely legible in indexed OCR). Original institutional account accessed through indexed full PDF. Claim is explicitly the mission’s own report.

sources.title: Orunodoi, February 1846, Assamese text and contemporary English headings
sources.note: Digital transcription, fourth and fifth pages of issue: গ্ৰহৰ বিবৰন / The Solar System; seven principal planets and four small planets; Shape of the Earth compares earth with a pomelo. Work landing page identifies collected second edition of volumes I to II, 1846 to 1847. Not a facsimile inspection.

sources.title: Namrata Sarmah, Textile Traditions of Northeast India (British Museum ITP, 2020)
sources.note: Paragraphs on songs, parent/child and mentor/apprentice transmission. This is explicitly a modern museum interpretation of continuing traditions, not a dated 1783 household survey.

proposedOverrides.summary: Late Ahom, Burmese and British phases in Assam, with a seriously misleading early atlas outline.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One regional narrative, no aliases. Existing Kamarupa and Burma cards remain distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1783 to 1800 polygon includes Thimphu, Paro and Punakha but excludes all checked Assam core cities. No 1800 to 1815 feature. 1815 to 1878 polygon contains Guwahati, Sivasagar and Jorhat but also Shillong, Silchar, Tawang, Itanagar, Kohima and Imphal. Public overview explicitly flags displacement, gap and overreach.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Period boundary 1819 selects documented Burmese predominance rather than first intervention. Ahom history begins much earlier than 1783. Restored tributary territory annexed 1838; 1878 is only a map cutoff.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Digital transcription of a dated Assamese periodical with its own English heading. No facsimile typography claim, no invented Ahom inscription.
